scores.claim_text: ARQQ has a firm fixed-price Qinetiq Space NV contract for QKD-satellite delivery by May 2022 and launch readiness review by July 2022.
scores.supports: edgar_fts.query_fulltext(search_term='Arqit Qinetiq', cutoff_date='2022-06-01') returned status_500 (transient). Filing internally discloses Qinetiq contract was signed 27-Jan-2020 with delivery May 2022 — i.e., delivery is essentially at the cutoff date but the company simultaneously says first satellite launches 'by 2023' on Virgin Orbit (LauncherOne, Newquay), which itself was an unproven UK-from-Cornwall launch site at this cutoff.
scores.M_value: Internal-consistency check: delivery milestone is at cutoff but launch slips to 2023; supply-chain dependence on a not-yet-proven UK launch service
scores.interpretation: Mode-B implied-verification: the timeline is internally fragile — a fixed-price 2020 contract for May-2022 satellite delivery is being followed by a 2023 launch on an unproven LauncherOne / Newquay service. Schedule risk is concentrated on counterparties (Qinetiq + Virgin Orbit) the company has limited control over, and is the gating event for the entire FQS / NATO narrative. Score MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY: not a J-Book defunding signal, but the load-bearing operational milestone has material execution risk that the framework's orthogonal-counterparty lens flags.

scores.claim_text: Capitalized development costs were $18.2M (FY21) vs $8.8M (FY20), with most expenditure treated as intangible asset rather than expensed R&D.
scores.supports: Filing notes 11: capitalized development costs $18,235,034 (FY21) up from $8,776,530 (FY20). Note 1: 'For the periods ended September 30, 2021, 2020 and 2019, there were no research costs reflected in the statement of comprehensive income. This is primarily due to the research phase being deemed as complete in 2018.' Going-concern note: only $8.7M cash at 30-Sep-2021 after a SPAC that grossed ~$96M (de-SPAC and PIPE) — heavy cash burn already.
scores.M_value: 100% of dev spend capitalised; $8.7M cash remaining after $96M raise; net loss $271.7M (driven by reverse-acquisition expense $155.5M).
scores.interpretation: Mode-B finding: aggressive IAS 38 capitalisation policy (zero research expense across three fiscal years because the 'research phase was deemed complete in 2018') combined with the satellite timeline (delivery May-2022, launch 2023) means $18.2M of intangibles are pre-revenue and untested. Cash position post-deSPAC is unexpectedly thin ($8.7M) given the $96M raise, due to ~$24M operating cash use in FY21. The framework flags this as MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY of the capital story, even without a J-Book signal.

summary.notes: At the 2022-06-01 cutoff, ARQQ does NOT name any specific U.S. DoD Program Element. The cohort's primary J-Book divergence pattern therefore does not have a sharp anchor here. Pentagon_jbook returns NOT_FOUND on all Arqit-specific queries; the adjacent AFRL Quantum Networking program is FUNDED_STEADY at FY22 but the primary contractor is IonQ (not Arqit). usaspending shows zero DoD awards under any Arqit name variant. The Mode-B (implied-verification) findings — Northrop Grumman counterparty silence (c5), satellite-timeline fragility (c8), and aggressive capitalisation + thin cash (c9) — are the framework's strongest 2022 signals; per the prompt these warrant MODERATE flags rather than SEVERE because the FY 2024-26 J-Book defundings that would crystallise the thesis are not yet visible. This is the honest 2022 view.
